title: Hou Hanshu (後漢書) 88, Xiyu Zhuan — the 166 CE embassy of 'Andun, King of Da Qin'
language_note: Classical Chinese. Hou Hanshu (Book of the Later Han) compiled by Fan Ye, 5th century CE, covering the Eastern Han period (25-220 CE); this chapter (88, Xiyu Zhuan / Chapter on the Western Regions) draws partly on the Weilüe.
date: compiled 5th century CE; records an event of 166 CE
original_text_excerpt: 至桓帝延熹九年，大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角、瑇瑁，始乃一通焉。
original_text_note: CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED 2026-08-22, against the Chinese Wikisource transcription of 後漢書/卷88 named in citation_original. The promise this field previously made — "cross-check against the authoritative Chinese Wikisource transcription during ingestion" — had never been kept, and it was kept only because the same promise on eastasia-01-weilue turned out to be hiding invented text. RESULT: GENUINE. 34 of the 36 characters are identical to the source. The two that differ are 獻/献 at position 20, a traditional/simplified pair and an artefact of the zh-hans view the source was read in, and 瑇/玳 at position 27 — variant characters for the same word, tortoiseshell, and NOT a simplification pair. That one is unresolved: settling it needs a traditional-script critical edition, and it is left flagged rather than silently normalised to whichever form looks tidier. The record keeps its own reading. Contrast eastasia-01-weilue, flagged identically by ingest.fidelity and found to be fabricated: the flag marked suspicion about both and distinguished neither.
reference_translation: In the ninth yanxi year [166 CE], during the reign of Emperor Huan, the king of Da Qin (the Roman Empire), Andun (Marcus Aurelius Antoninus), sent envoys from beyond the frontiers through Rinan (Commandery on the central Vietnamese coast), to offer elephant tusks, rhinoceros horn, and turtle shell. This was the very first time there was [direct] communication [between the two countries]. The tribute brought was neither precious nor rare, raising suspicion that the accounts [of the 'envoys'] might be exaggerated.
translation_source: John E. Hill, '"Chapter on the Western Regions" from Hou Hanshu 88', draft annotated translation, University of Washington Silk Road Seattle project.
notes: Records what Chinese sources present as the first direct Rome-China diplomatic contact (166 CE), traditionally identified with Marcus Aurelius. 'Andun' (安敦) as a transliteration of 'Antoninus' is itself a good micro-example of cross-lingual proper-noun handling for the translation/back-translation pipeline (Pillar 1, §6).

subject_places.name: Rinan
subject_places.note: 日南, the commandery on the central Vietnamese coast the embassy arrived through — 自日南徼外, 'from beyond the frontier of Rinan'. Pleiades is a Greco-Roman gazetteer and holds nothing here; this is GeoNames territory, and the GeoNames reader is the outstanding Block A item. Promote to a named place when it exists.

subject_places.name: Da Qin
subject_places.note: 大秦, whose king 安敦 sent the envoys. Same reasoning as `eastasia-01-weilue`: a polity with no gazetteer entry, and the identification with Rome is the gloss's rather than the record's. Luoyang, the court the tribute was offered to, is NOT named in this passage and is deliberately not placed.
